summary: Central, oldest lens fibres; yellows and browns with nuclear sclerosis, which raises scatter and absorbs blue light.

relative_size.note: Nucleus boundary as a fraction of the lens half-dimensions.

scatter.note: Extra backscatter of a clear nucleus. Render-calibrated.

density.note: Nuclear opacity; 1.0 is a dense brunescent nucleus.

scatter_colour.note: Colour of light scattered back by the nucleus.

milky_scatter.note: Near-white scatter per unit density, from the opacity's large particles, which gives a nuclear cataract its milky haze. Render-calibrated, not clinically validated.

absorption_tint.note: Per-channel absorption per unit density; blue is absorbed most, so dense nuclei look brown.

provenance.source: Render calibration; LOCS III: Chylack et al. (1993)
